Add my `.xonshrc` here
```bash
# XONSH WIZARD START
source-zsh --login True "echo loading xonsh foreign shell"
xontrib load coreutils prompt_ret_code whole_word_jumping
# XONSH WIZARD END

$PROMPT = '{env_name}{BOLD_GREEN}{user}@{hostname}{BOLD_CYAN} \n{cwd}{branch_color}{curr_branch: {}}{RESET} \n{ret_code_color}{ret_code}{BOLD_BLUE}{prompt_end}{RESET} '
$COMPLETIONS_CONFIRM = True

# I commented this line below out to prevent the shell from breaking
# execx($(starship init xonsh))
```
What version of Xonsh are you running? If memory serves, there was a breaking change in the init recently.

> What version of Xonsh are you running?

My Xonsh version is 0.11.0, which is released on 18 Nov 2021 according to the GitHub page.

> If memory serves, there was a breaking change in the init recently.

And that would make sense since the support for Xonsh was first introduced on 26 Aug 2021, hoping for an update soon.

Hm, I must have gotten my wires crossed, because I can't find that PR in the logs. I can only assume for now that I got it confused with the elvish update (which did happen a few months ago).

I trialed this with your `rc.xsh` and was able to get this down to `xontrib load coreutils` being the offending line. I also think I know what the issue is (some part of Xonsh assumes that objects have a `pid` property, but the entry is a `ProcProxyThread`, which does not have a PID), but I don't know when the offending code snuck in, so I'll do some bisecting to see if I can narrow it down.

Okay.

So this somehow has to do with external prompt commands that take too long to render **and** the presence of coreutils in the rc.xsh.

Could you confirm for me that the following Xonshrc crashes for you? (You might need to rapidly mash "ENTER" to see a failure/crash). And if you comment out the first line, the errors go away?

If so, we have an issue to report upstream.

```
xontrib load coreutils # Comment out to fix issue

$XONSH_SHOW_TRACEBACK = True

def prompt():
    return $(sleep 0.5 | echo """Prompt>""" | cat)

$PROMPT = prompt
```
